scope: Operational continuation only; original 406-identity source, eight exact methods, forty full independent records and 484 predecessor identities unchanged.
rules: Never invoke before original run outcome exists with active_children=0, source_unchanged=true and status=checkpoint. Failed/interrupted original attempts require separate diagnosis/correction, not this protocol.

Before continuation execution, publish and freeze exact SHA256 bindings for every closed original output file, exact accepted capacity/paid raw inputs, original 406 source identities and this operational protocol/module/binding. No active logs enter the binding.

Use original frozen evaluator stage CLI without modifying its source, runtime, auditor or actual test bodies. At most four disjoint missing record workers; all forty exact reports before at most two missing actual-method workers; all eight exact passing results before unchanged finish alone.

Existing record reports, method results and prefix outputs are immutable and must match their frozen hashes. Existing passing stages never rerun. Every prior launch must have a matching closed job with exit_code=0 and passed=true.

Fresh exclusive operational output and per-child logs. Each launch/closure verifies original source, operational freeze, all bound prefix files and all accepted raw inputs. New stage outputs must validate exact key/method/source/raw hash, not counts alone.

Require explicit owner plus current running public state and a lease with more than 300 seconds remaining before each launch. Require an explicit absolute UTC stop time after start and no more than 30 minutes later; record it in immutable plan. Stop new launches on first child/verification failure, STOP marker, deadline, or ownership/lease change. Wait active children naturally; no signals, namespace changes, automatic retries or paid input regeneration.

Write exact closed job metadata, logs/hashes and outcome. Status checkpoint is not acceptance; acceptance requires original unchanged finish and all original conditions. Subsequent continuation requires a fresh numbered output and prospectively bound complete prior-output prefix; no reuse of an existing operational run.
